experiment.title: Conditional negative-share information and LSEG transfer
experiment.objective: Test directly whether negative-story share retains next-open return information after controlling for mean continuous sentiment and story count, then transfer the unchanged estimand to separate LSEG time blocks.
experiment.evidence_role: retrospective conditional test and non-pooled temporal robustness

inputs.source_regimes: FNSPID and Reuters LSEG remain separate and are never pooled

estimand.unit: daily cross-sectional coefficient followed by a time-series mean
estimand.outcome: within-session average-tie percentile rank of next-open return, centred at zero
regressors: within-session centred percentile rank of mean continuous sentiment
within-session centred percentile rank of negative-story share
within-session centred percentile rank of log(1 + story count)
estimand.inference: OLS intercept on daily coefficients with Newey-West HAC lag 5

fnspid_core_test.supports_beyond_mean_claim_if: coefficient is negative and the two-sided HAC p-value is below 0.05

lseg_primary_transfer.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg across two two-sided p-values at q=0.05
lseg_primary_transfer.supports_portability_if: both coefficients are negative and both survive the two-test correction

lseg_scorer_sensitivity.role: direction and magnitude sensitivity only; cannot rescue a failed FinBERT transfer

families_and_gates.univariate_context: Report the already-declared nine-rule daily IC table for each LSEG block without using it to select or reverse a rule.

economic_context.negative_share_book: Reuse the existing centred cross-sectional-rank, gross-one, dollar-neutral h1 convention with 10 bps per side and final liquidation.
economic_context.role: context only; no new trading-rule selection

claim_boundaries: The FNSPID and LSEG outcomes were opened before this specification.
A significant negative-share univariate IC is not evidence beyond the mean unless the frozen conditional coefficient also passes.
A null or opposite-signed LSEG result narrows portability; it does not license scorer, sign, threshold, horizon, universe, or cost retuning.
Failure to reject is not proof that the effect is zero; report coefficients and intervals.
Gemma is a sensitivity analysis, not a second opportunity to pass the primary gate.
